lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: a great business, but this lens's own price test fails and the price is 131% above the fair value of ₹802.

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.w: Doesn't apply: borrowing is the raw material of a lender's business.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: 20 dividends in 10 years with no gap longer than 18 months.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +53%.

ch.w: You pay ₹37 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)

cw: 2 of 3 methods within ±25% of the fair value

rs.t: Price ₹1,850 is 134% above the absolute value of ₹790 (🛡️ Strict view, used for this verdict) (1 of 3 methods say cheap, 2 say expensive)
Decisions timeline 26/100 over the last 3 years
Debt is 6.51× its own money – better than 9% of NBFCs & housing finance
Earns 19% a year on shareholders' money – better than 82% of NBFCs & housing finance
Income growing 33% a year – better than 82% of NBFCs & housing finance

v4.ll: Passes Fisher, Mukherjea-style checks; great business but price not right for Graham, Buffett, Agrawal; fails F-score, Kedia-style checks
ch: Can only reach Accumulate or Buy if the quality score rises to 70 (now 69); drops to Avoid below 50.
Moves to Trim above ₹1,043 (30% over fair value).

Any new serious red flag (auditor resigns mid-term, pledge above 25%, SEBI order, negative net worth, weak cash conversion together with high accruals, distress with interest cover below 1.5×) moves it straight to Avoid.

va.pw: Banks and NBFCs: justified P/B and dividends (their cash-flow family), plus own and peer P/B.

dcf.w: Not used for lenders: their cash flow is mostly loans going out and deposits coming in.

epv.w: Not used for lenders (interest is their cost of goods, so EBIT doesn't mean the same thing).

ddm.n: Floor check: all future dividends at a 3% payout. Shown, not counted.

peer_ev_ebitda.w: Not used for financial companies (debt is their raw material).

peer_ev_sales.w: Not used for financial companies (debt is their raw material).

mid_ev_ebitda.w: Needs EBITDA margins and sector EV/EBITDA.

sotp.w: Needs segment / listed-stake data (Stage 5 Company Reader); holding-company discount 20–40% (PROXY) will apply.

nav.w: Needs land bank / investment values from annual reports (Stage 5).

replacement.w: Needs capacity (tonnes) and today's cost per tonne from investor presentations (Stage 5).

ROE at least 15% (median of recent years; lender's version of ROCE)
